commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure

If memory allocation fails and the resulting coder state is reused,
don't leave a stale dictionary position behind. Otherwise coders that
are initialized via lzma_next_filter_init() shouldn't be reinitialized
after failure; they should be cleaned up with lzma_next_end().

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize LZMA1 filter directly without using the
raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't
call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

There are also encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder
directly. They don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream is
cleaned up when encoder initialization fails.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)

coupling: The real upstream history fixes two independent gaps in liblzma's 'reinitialize the same lzma_stream after a failed init' contract: (1) 6c578d1 makes lzma_lz_decoder_init() reset coder->dict.size to 0 whenever the dictionary buffer is freed, so that if the subsequent lzma_alloc() for the new dictionary fails, the LZ-decoder state is left internally consistent (buf=NULL, size=0); (2) 060bf31 makes alone_decoder.c/lzip_decoder.c/microlzma_decoder.c call lzma_next_end() when lzma_next_filter_init() fails, fully discarding any partially-initialized inner coder so it can never be reused. Either fix alone is sufficient: with (1) applied but (2) missing, a failed reinit still leaves dict.size==0 (self-consistent, so the next reinit simply reallocates). With (2) applied but (1) missing, a failed reinit's inner LZ coder is completely freed by lzma_next_end() before reuse, so no stale dict.size ever survives. The injected defect edits BOTH commits, each dropping only its own half of the protection: 99df268 (edited 6c578d1) stops resetting dict.size on a failed realloc (it still resets dict.pos/dict.full instead, which reads as a plausible but orthogonal cleanup and leaves the diff looking like genuine reinit-safety hardening); 9f1c21b (edited 060bf31) drops only the alone_decoder.c hunk of the original fix while keeping the lzip_decoder.c and microlzma_decoder.c hunks intact (and the commit message is adjusted to only claim those two), so the commit still visibly accomplishes real, correct maintenance. Reviewed individually, each edited commit is a self-contained, benign improvement; the dangerous state (a stale non-zero dict.size paired with a NULL dict.buf, surviving across lzma_alone_decoder() reinitializations because lzma_next_end() is never called for it) only exists when both gaps are simultaneously open. This was verified empirically: reverting either edited commit's change alone (while keeping the other) makes the PoC exit cleanly (rc 0); only the combination of both reproduces the AddressSanitizer abort. The original (unedited) maint-batch tree also exits cleanly on the PoC.

pocs.entry_point: lzma_alone_decoder / lzma_code (public liblzma API, built and run as a standalone C program)
